A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MagicDriveDiT and contain readable main text, references, and complete appendices. Rendering resolved extraction issues in diagrams, supporting comparison of the methods, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video generation experiments, ablations, VAE reconstruction measurements, and qualitative comparisons, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Waymo and mixed-dataset results, contextual-control examples, and a human consistency evaluation.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 introduces MLLM-based caption regeneration using each video's middle frame, with prompts separating contextual descriptions from geometric controls. This extends the conditioning pipeline; the MVDiT architecture, spatial-temporal encoders, flow-matching objective, and original training stages remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1's experiments use nuScenes. v2 adds Waymo fine-tuning and joint Waymo/nuScenes training, extending coverage to different environments, three-camera videos, and different semantic categories. Figure 5 also demonstrates richer contextual controls beyond the earlier weather/time examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the matched video, image, encoder, VAE, and rollout comparisons. The new human study reuses MagicDrive; the added Waymo results introduce no additional comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct training and evaluation protocols: Waymo fine-tuning from Stage 3, joint-dataset training, and paired human consistency judgments. Waymo uses 798/202 training/validation clips, 10 Hz annotations, and three retained front views. The original nuScenes metrics and training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a focused human assessment of multi-frame/multi-view consistency, and Figure 5 adds contextual-control cases. Existing encoder, VAE, resolution/length, and rollout analyses remain; the training-efficiency analysis moves to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v2's human preference percentages are point results; no uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds mixed-dataset model FVDs of 105.17 on Waymo and 74.30 on nuScenes, plus human preferences of 95.83% for MagicDriveDiT, 2.50% for MagicDrive, and 1.67% ties. These add distinct result families alongside contextual-control examples. Existing benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged; 74.30 versus Table 2's 94.84 involves different training.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, scene-condition definitions, and flow-matching equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. v2 adds explanatory reasoning but no new formal assumptions, propositions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 adds caption-based contextual control as an explicit contribution and emphasizes adapting DiT/3D VAE through MVDiT and geometric conditioning. Its headline 848×1600×241 capability was already stated and illustrated in v1's appendix, so its promotion does not establish a new capability.

C2.justification: v2 newly hypothesizes that repeating globally reduced conditions causes trailing and explains how selective captions avoid conflicting controls. Section 4.2 also changes v1's negative GFLOPs–FID correlation to lower GFLOPs giving better FID, reversing the stated relationship. The substantial inference-cost limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds captioning guidance, Waymo preprocessing and semantic categories, and a one-day, 1k-plus-step fine-tuning budget. Existing optimizer, hardware, and sampling details remain. However, v1's explicit disclosure that perception evaluators were pretrained on real data is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Cosmos, the GPT-4o system card, and Waymo, while removing Align Your Latents, Animate Anyone, Open-Sora-Plan, and DynamiCrafter. Positioning now emphasizes adapting the established DiT/3D-VAE framework for driving controls; most related-work relationships remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, much of the introduction, and method exposition are substantially rewritten. Architecture and geometric control receive separate subsections, captioning receives a new subsection, progressive and mixed-data training discussions are consolidated, and the efficiency discussion moves to the appendix.

P2.justification: Figure 5's training illustration is replaced by contextual-control examples, and a human-evaluation chart is added as appendix Figure II. Figures 1–2 are revised, and the training-speed table moves from main Table 4 to appendix Table II. Most existing visual evidence and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The captioning procedure, Waymo experiments, and human consistency assessment broaden the paper's applicability and provide useful evidence beyond v1's nuScenes experiments. The gains are limited by missing human-study sample counts and uncertainty, sparse joint-training details, and the reversed GFLOPs–FID explanation. Existing benchmark evidence remains intact, supporting a modest net improvement rather than a substantial one.
